description: The dead-code half of the policy. The real work is exponential backoff with caps and an attempt ceiling, and the guard that implements the ceiling also returns early on `fatal`. The switch below it swaps its old `default` arm for an explicit `case "fatal"` arm in the same edit, so the diff adds a branch the guard two lines above already makes unreachable. The caps and the comment on THROTTLE_CAP_MS are must-not-flag: the comment records where the number came from, and the two Math.min lines are the logic work.

evidence_trace: src/queue/retry.ts:9 returns null when `kind === "fatal"` before the switch
src/queue/retry.ts:17-18 adds `case "fatal": return null;` inside the switch, which no kind reaches
FailureKind has exactly three members, so the switch's remaining two arms are exhaustive without it
finding.failure_scenario: The next reader of the switch sees two places that decide what fatal means, changes the one that never runs, and ships a fix that does nothing.
finding.model_authored_prose: The `case "fatal"` arm at retry.ts:17 is unreachable: the guard at line 9 already returns null for fatal. Delete the arm so the switch says what still varies.

prContext.description: Retries were linear and unbounded. Transient failures now back off exponentially to a 30s cap, throttled ones to the upstream's 60s retry-after maximum, and every kind stops after six attempts.
